speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing swelling in your right knee and have a family history of similar issues; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you recall any specific injury? Additionally, does the pain worsen with activity or is it constant?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease. The clinical picture of an 18-month-old boy with right knee swelling (referred pain from the hip), no traumatic injury, and a family history of similar hip issues is highly suggestive of this condition. I will now request imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvis_XRay_AP AND Pelvis_XRay_Lateral.
